page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.4-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the 64-bit Arm architecture. The instance is powered by the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor family and provides 8 physical cores allocated on a dedicated basis. Because each core runs a single thread, the instance exposes 8 dedicated vCPUs with no resource sharing from simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 32.0 GB, providing an even ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

Hardware expansion and peripheral options reflect a standardized virtual environment. The instance includes no integrated hardware accelerators or discrete GPUs. Local disk storage is not bundled with the instance, which requires all persistent operating system and data disks to be attached via network-attached block storage services. Networking capabilities include one complimentary public IPv4 address assigned to the virtual machine.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio offers balanced resource distribution without over-indexing on memory or compute density. By utilizing single-threaded dedicated Arm cores, the instance provides steady computational execution devoid of thread contention issues. Workload profiles that align with this system configuration include microservices architectures, web application hosting, build systems, containerized runtimes, and intermediate caching layers that operate natively on arm64 instruction sets.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.4-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the arm64 architecture. It is powered by the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor family, providing 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, resulting in 8 vCPUs. The instance includes 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per physical core. There are no attached hardware accelerators or dedicated GPUs, and no local storage is bundled, requiring workloads to rely entirely on external block storage volumes. Network provisioning includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. The dedicated core configuration avoids noisy neighbor interference typical of simultaneous multithreading environments, offering consistent compute execution per core. This hardware profile is appropriate for general-purpose application workloads, intermediate container hosting, web application serving, backend microservices, and continuous integration pipelines that benefit from native 64-bit Arm execution.
